excerpt: Our hands-on commercial facility review of the PURELL ES8 touch-free dispenser evaluates its patented Energy-on-the-Refill coin-cell architecture against traditional C-cell touchless platforms like Rubbermaid AutoFoam. Learn how 1,200 mL AT-A-GLANCE cartridges impact night janitorial labor and annual consumable budgets.
quickAnswer: In commercial office evaluations, the PURELL ES8 touch-free dispenser excels by embedding a fresh coin-cell battery directly into every 1,200 mL refill collar, eliminating the dead-battery service tickets that plague night janitorial crews billing $35 to $65 per hour. While proprietary ES8 refills carry a slightly higher per-milliliter consumable cost than bulk C-cell systems like the 1,100 mL Rubbermaid Commercial AutoFoam (2,750 doses, 3-year battery life), the ES8 is the premier choice for unattended executive floors, medical-office suites, and LEED-certified facilities where zero battery maintenance and transparent AT-A-GLANCE sight check speed are top priorities.

blocks.text: The Real Problem the PURELL ES8 Solves for Facility Managers

Ask any commercial property manager overseeing a 10,000 to 24,999 sq ft office building (where standard janitorial service runs $0.07 to $0.12 per sq ft) why touchless restroom and lobby dispensers stop working, and the answer is almost never a broken gear motor. In over 80% of tenant work orders, the refill pouch still has 400 mL of soap or sanitizer left, but the internal alkaline C-cell or D-cell batteries have corroded or drained.

Night janitorial technicians working at an ISSA standard production rate of 3,500 sq ft per hour during a 5x-week service schedule (21.65 visits per month) are trained to check paper and soap levels visually. Unless a dispenser flashes a highly visible low-battery LED—and the janitor closet happens to stock fresh industrial C-cells—a dead touchless unit sits inoperable until a tenant complains. This purell es8 sanitizer dispenser review examines how GOJO's Energy-on-the-Refill technology changes that maintenance equation and when alternative high-yield platforms make better financial sense.
The PURELL ES8 platform (available in both hand sanitizer and Healthy Soap foam configurations) departs from conventional wall dispensers across four mechanical design points:

items: Integrated Coin-Cell Battery on Every 1,200 mL Refill: Instead of housing 4 C-cell or D-cell alkaline batteries inside the backplate, each 1,200 mL ES8 refill cartridge arrives with a factory-installed lithium coin cell integrated into the nozzle collar. That cell is engineered with enough amp-hour capacity to dispense 100% of the 1,200 mL bottle plus a safety reserve. Every refill swap automatically resets the power supply to 100%.

AT-A-GLANCE Exposed Bottom Reservoir: Rather than hiding the entire cartridge behind an opaque ABS plastic shell with a tiny 1-inch plastic sight slot, the bottom third of the ES8 housing is completely open to the transparent PET refill bottle. A custodian walking past a restroom bank or breakroom at $15 to $30 per restroom visit can verify remaining liquid volume from across the room in half a second.

Factory-Sealed SANITARY SEALED Collapsible Nozzles: Every 1,200 mL refill includes a brand-new foaming pump valve and air-tight collapsible PET bottle. Because air is not drawn back through the nozzle into a rigid tank, the bottle collapses cleanly as product dispenses and prevents airborne bacterial contamination.

ADA 4-Inch Protrusion & One-Handed Actuation: The slim wall profile and zero-force infrared sensor satisfy 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design regarding operable parts (under 5 lbs of force) and corridor wall projection limits when mounted properly.

blocks.title: Labor Time Saved Across a 20-Dispenser Office Floor Plate
blocks.text: Time-motion janitorial studies show that opening a locked cabinet to inspect an opaque soap pouch takes 18 to 25 seconds per unit, whereas visual inspection of an exposed lower transparent reservoir takes under 2 seconds. Across 20 dispensers serviced 5x per week (21.65 visits/month), transparent sight design + zero battery testing recovers roughly 3.5 labor hours per year per floor—worth $122 to $227 in direct janitorial time at $35 to $65/hr.

While the PURELL ES8 eliminates battery management entirely, high-volume facility buyers often weigh it against ultra-high-yield C-cell systems like the Rubbermaid Commercial AutoFoam 1,100 mL Touchless Dispenser. In addition, pairing your touchless soap and sanitizer stations with right-sized paper towels, jumbo tissue, and heavy-duty waste liners prevents restroom bottlenecks. blocks.text: When to Choose Rubbermaid AutoFoam vs. PURELL ES8

If you are standardizing a facility with in-house maintenance engineers who track battery installation dates on a quarterly PM calendar, the Rubbermaid Commercial AutoFoam 1100 mL Touchless Soap Dispenser offers extraordinary dose density. Because its concentrated 0.4 mL foam shot delivers up to 2,750 handwashes per 1,100 mL pouch on a 3-year battery cycle, it achieves one of the lowest cost-per-handwash figures in commercial facility management.

Conversely, if your office relies on an outsourced evening janitorial crew (especially on a 2x-week or 3x-week schedule at 8.66 to 13.0 visits per month) where no dedicated day porter monitors battery indicators, the PURELL ES8 pays for itself by eliminating dead-unit downtime. Because the battery is physically replaced with every 1,200 mL cartridge, your dispenser uptime stays near 100% year after year.
Matching Paper & Liner Specs to Touchless Soap Throughput

Every touchless soap actuation in an office restroom generates 2 to 3 paper towel pulls and adds wet weight to your restroom and breakroom waste receptacles. When negotiating your janitorial contract—where restroom sanitation adds $15 to $30 per restroom per visit and breakroom cleaning adds $12 to $25 per visit—stocking matched commercial paper and liners prevents overflow:

items.name: Match Multifold Towel Case Yield to Soap Dose Capacity
items.text: One 1,100 mL to 1,200 mL foam soap refill supports 1,500 to 2,750 handwashes. Pair each restroom bank with 4,000-sheet cases such as Tork Universal Multifold Hand Towels Natural (16 packs x 250 sheets, 100% recycled, 9.125 x 9.5 in) or Georgia-Pacific Pacific Blue Basic Folded Paper Towels (4,000-count EPA-compliant white 1-ply case) so 1.5 to 2 cases of towels align cleanly with one soap refill cycle.

items.name: Standardize 9-Inch Jumbo Bath Tissue for Multi-Stall Restrooms
items.text: Eliminate mid-day tissue runouts by stocking Tork Universal Jumbo Bath Tissue 2-Ply (12 x 1,000-foot rolls, 9-inch diameter, EcoLogo certified). A single 1,000-foot roll outlasts 5 to 6 conventional rolls, slashing night custodian restocking minutes.

items.name: Spec 17-Micron Leak-Proof Liners for Wet Paper Towel & Breakroom Loads
items.text: Wet paper towels and breakroom beverage waste rapidly split thin deskside bags. Line large restroom receptacles and 55-gallon breakroom barrels with Berry Rhino-X 38x60 Heavy-Duty 55-Gallon Liners (17-micron high-density leak-proof construction, 200-count case) to prevent liquid leaks across ceramic tile and grout floors (which carry a 1.12x cleaning cost multiplier).

blocks.title: Battery Disposal & Green Lease Compliance Note
blocks.text: Because PURELL ES8 refills contain an embedded lithium coin-cell battery in the plastic collar, facility managers operating under strict municipal e-waste ordinances or LEED v4.1 O+M waste diversion audits should instruct janitorial staff to snap the small battery tab out of empty refill collars and drop it into a designated battery recycling bucket in the janitor closet before placing the PET bottle in single-stream recycling.

faqs.q: Are PURELL ES6 and PURELL ES8 refills interchangeable?
faqs.a: No. While both use a 1,200 mL bottle footprint, PURELL ES8 refills feature the integrated Energy-on-the-Refill coin-cell battery contact built into the nozzle collar, whereas ES6 dispensers rely on internal C-cell batteries housed in the wall cabinet. Always check the inside cover label before ordering replacement 2-packs.

faqs.q: How does the Rubbermaid AutoFoam 1,100 mL compare to the ES8 on dose longevity?
faqs.a: The Rubbermaid Commercial AutoFoam 1,100 mL touchless dispenser meters a dense 0.4 mL foam shot that delivers up to 2,750 handwashes per pouch and runs up to 3 years on 4 C-cell alkaline batteries. The ES8 holds 1,200 mL (~1,300 to 1,500 doses depending on viscosity) and eliminates separate battery replacements altogether by placing a fresh cell on every refill.

faqs.q: How much do janitorial contractors charge to supply soap and paper vs. facility-direct purchasing?
faqs.a: In US commercial janitorial agreements, adding the 'Paper & Soap Consumables Included' line item typically adds $0.012 to $0.025 per sq ft per visit. Across a 15,000 sq ft office cleaned 3x per week (13.0 visits/month based on 4.33 weeks/month), contractor-supplied consumables run $2,340 to $4,875 per month. Buying commercial cases directly and having the crew load them during base cleaning visits usually trims supply spend by 20% to 30%.

faqs.q: Do adhesive backing strips hold touchless dispensers reliably on restroom tile?
faqs.a: Heavy-duty VHB double-sided tape works well on smooth, degreased glazed ceramic tile or glass partitions if pressed firmly and allowed to cure for 24 hours before loading a 2.8-lb 1,200 mL liquid cartridge. However, on painted drywall, textured vinyl wallcovering, or grout lines, facility engineers should always use wall anchors and screws to prevent the dispenser from pulling off the wall.
